description: Phase 4b gate — WAL write-side + incremental commit. Per spec/wal.spec.md § 'Phase 4b — WAL write-side + incremental commit'. Activation via LEAP_WAL_APPEND=1; salts pinned via LEAP_WAL_SALT_OVERRIDE for byte-deterministic fixtures. Covers: session activation + header emission, single-commit frame append, multi-commit frame append + recovery-on-reopen, uncommitted-tail discard, wal-absent-after-checkpoint, and the Phase 3d fallback when LEAP_WAL_APPEND is unset. Both C and Rust builds MUST produce byte-identical WAL bytes for identical inputs.

schema.case: inherits phase4a.json schema plus new fields:
schema.wal_append: bool — default true when absent. Sets LEAP_WAL_APPEND=1 for the case.
schema.wal_salt_hex: string — 16 hex characters; 8 for salt-1 + 8 for salt-2 (big-endian u32 each). Required when wal_append is true.
schema.inspect_after_close: object — assertions about on-disk artifacts after db_close: wal_absent (bool), main_db_has_page_count (int).
schema.step.commit_label: string — triggers close+snapshot+reopen; records the WAL contents under this label.
schema.step.expect.wal_last_commit_page_count: int — db_size_after_commit of the last frame.
schema.expected_wal_hex_by_commit: object — label -> full expected hex bytes of the WAL file at that commit point.

cases.name: wal-append-disabled-phase3d-fallback
cases.description: Regression: with wal_append=false, behaviour is the Phase 3d atomic-rename commit. No <path>-wal is ever created.

cases.name: wal-append-single-commit-emits-frames-and-checkpoints-on-close
cases.description: With LEAP_WAL_APPEND=1, a single commit-unit (close) produces a <path>-wal with one frame per dirty page. After close, the WAL is absorbed into the main DB and unlinked. Reopen sees the merged state.

cases.name: wal-append-multi-commit-recovery-on-reopen
cases.description: Two separate commits (close/reopen cycles) each write to the WAL. The second reopen's Phase 4a+4b recovery walks both commits' frames, overlays them, checkpoints to main DB, unlinks WAL. Final state = post-both-commits.

program.sql: CREATE TABLE t (a INTEGER, b INTEGER);

cases.name: wal-append-bulk-insert-grows-dirty-set-proportionally
cases.description: A bulk insert of 500 rows produces multiple dirty pages. The WAL frame count reflects the number of changed/grown pages. On reopen, all rows survive.

program.sql: SELECT id FROM t WHERE id = 250;

cases.name: wal-append-uncommitted-tail-is-discarded-on-open
cases.description: A pre-existing <path>-wal file has a valid header but the tail is truncated mid-frame. Phase 4b recovery halts at the truncated frame and discards it; no error is raised (treated as 'uncommitted'). The main DB is opened normally; since the WAL had no committed-marker frame before the truncation, the engine sees only main-DB state.

cases.name: wal-append-empty-session-no-wal-on-close
cases.description: A WAL-append session that performs no mutations produces no committed frames. On close, the empty WAL (header only) is absorbed by the checkpoint (a no-op overlay) and unlinked. Main DB on disk is unchanged.
